title: Chop & Shape a Sample
blurb: Turn one long sample into playable pieces, then reshape them with gate, loop, reverse, and pitch.

steps.title: Pick your source
body: Load or record a longer sample onto a pad — a few bars of music, a spoken phrase, or a drum break.
Play it once and listen for the moments you actually want: the downbeat, a vocal word, a chord change.
steps.checkpoint: One pad holds the full-length sample.
steps.tip: Longer sources give you more to work with, but eat memory fast. A 4-bar loop is plenty for a first pass.

steps.title: Set the start and end points
body: With the pad selected, press START/END.
CTRL 1 moves the start point; CTRL 2 moves the end point.
Trim the start onto the transient you want to hear the instant you press the pad — no lead-in silence.
Move the end just past the tail of that section.
steps.checkpoint: The pad triggers exactly the slice you intended, with no dead air at the front.
steps.tip: Hold the pad and adjust while it plays. Your ears will find the transient faster than your eyes will.

steps.title: Gate versus loop
body: GATE makes the pad sound only while you hold it, and stop when you release — ideal for stabs and chops you want to play rhythmically.
LOOP makes the pad repeat continuously — ideal for drum loops and sustained textures.
Toggle each one on your chop and play it a few times to feel the difference.
steps.checkpoint: You can start and stop the sound with your finger under GATE, and leave it running under LOOP.
steps.tip: Gate is what makes finger drumming with melodic chops feel expressive — short taps become staccato, held taps ring out.

steps.title: Reverse and re-pitch
body: Press REVERSE to play the slice backwards. Reversed tails make natural transitions and risers.
Use the pitch and speed controls to shift the slice up or down.
Pitching a drum break down thickens it; pitching a vocal up changes its character completely.
steps.checkpoint: The same source now gives you several usable variations.
steps.tip: Whether pitch changes affect playback length depends on the mode you are in — try both and pick whichever keeps your loop in time.

steps.title: Spread the chops across pads
body: Copy the sample to several pads and give each one a different start and end point, so each pad is a different slice of the same source.
Lay them out so the slices you play together sit under comfortable fingers — order them musically, not just left to right.
Now you can perform the sample instead of just replaying it.
steps.checkpoint: Four pads, four slices, one source — playable as a phrase.
steps.tip: Once the layout feels good, resample your performance to a single pad. That is the Resample guide, and it is how chopped beats get built.
